about: Data of Learn lesson M8 (deciding before the uncertainty resolves: stochastic and robust optimization). A fictional windy zone of the Plains region: illustrative round numbers in 2025 dollars, not the inputs or results of any study. The wind blocks are rounded from SPP's 2025 hourly wind shape (EIA-930, town_year.json) scaled to EIA's 2025 U.S. wind capacity factor (cf_targets.json). The reference block holds the lesson's results, solved with this model in HiGHS; the lab notebook checks its answers against them.

zone.name: the windy zone
zone.note: Illustrative: the zone's lines and local demand take up to 1,000 MW of wind in any hour; wind above that is surplus, curtailed unless an electrolyzer uses it.

wind.note: Illustrative: 3,000 MW of wind built, 4,000 MW more planned; how much of the planned wind gets built is the uncertainty.

scenarios.label: None of the planned wind built
Half of the planned wind built
All of the planned wind built

blocks.note: The 8,760 hours of 2025 sorted by the wind fleet's output (a duration curve) and cut into five blocks; each block's capacity factor is the mean of its hours, rounded to three decimals. SPP's hourly wind shape (EIA-930) scaled to 33.8%, EIA's 2025 capacity factor for U.S. utility-scale wind (Electric Power Monthly, Table 6.07.B), with LX.townProfile's method "scale"; the windiest hour reaches 64% of capacity.

source.label: EIA-930 (SPP 2025) and EIA Electric Power Monthly, Table 6.07.B

electrolyzer.note: Illustrative: $80,000 per MW a year, the annualized capital and fixed upkeep; 18 kg of hydrogen per MWh (about 55 kWh per kg). It runs only on surplus wind.

hydrogen.note: Illustrative: industry takes 54,000 kg of hydrogen every hour; what the electrolyzer does not make comes from gas reformers at $1.50 per kg.

reference.about: Reference results, solved with the lesson's model in HiGHS. Costs in $ a year (2025 dollars), sizes in MW.
